biothings.name: extrinsic asthma
biothings.definition: A chronic asthma that is triggered by an allergen and that is characterized by an immune system overreaction to a harmless substance, such as pollen or dust, with the subsequent release of immunoglobin E (IgE) antibodies. [DOID:0080811]

biothings.name: childhood onset asthma
biothings.synonyms: asthma of childhood, childhood asthma, paediatric asthma, pediatric asthma

biothings.name: environmental induced asthma
biothings.definition: An intrinsic asthma that is characterized by exposure to tobacco smoke and other inflammatory gasses or particulate matter. [DOID:0080819]

kegg.description: Asthma with nasal polyps and aspirin intolerance

opentargets.name: asthma
opentargets.description: A bronchial disease that is characterized by chronic inflammation and narrowing of the airways, which is caused by a combination of environmental and genetic factors resulting in recurring periods of wheezing (a whistling sound while breathing), chest tightness, shortness of breath, mucus production and coughing. The symptoms appear due to a variety of triggers such as allergens, irritants, respiratory infections, weather changes, exercise, stress, reflux disease, medications, foods and emotional anxiety.

opentargets.name: allergic asthma
opentargets.description: A asthma with a basis in a pathological type I hypersensitivity reaction.

opentargets.name: age of onset of asthma
opentargets.description: The age at which asthma manifestations first appear.

opentargets.name: atopic asthma
opentargets.description: An asthma that is characterized by symptoms that are triggered by an allergic reaction caused by inhaled allergens such as dust mite allergen, pet dander, pollen and mold.
